directions.brief: Subject built on P1 Section drawing; drawing language: typeset diagram.
Subject built on P2 Diagram + trace; drawing language: orthographic elevation.
Subject built on P3 Trace as subject; drawing language: survey plan.
Subject built on P4 Stack in depth; drawing language: patent section.
Subject built on P11 Instrument stack; drawing language: hidden-line isometric. This pattern is outside the category's column: say why this machine is the exception, or say plainly it doesn't fit.

variants.subject: The cutting stylus caught mid-cut in a textbook cross-section of the lacquer blank, its V sunk into the coat and a swarf thread coiling off behind it.
controls: cut: shape (node 0, the groove under the stylus) - the V deepens from ~7 to ~22 px and its point bottoms out into a flat floor as the cutter saturates (1.4 to ~9 px flat); the stylus (node 1) rides down with it.

groove: position - the blank slides under the fixed stylus: the rim bevel runs out to the left and the uncut inner lacquer's break line comes in from the right (~160-170 px), so more cut grooves trail the stylus.
wear: count - chips and rounded lips appear on the grooves already cut, left of the stylus (0 to ~14 marks); none at 0.
rumble: shape - the platter line under the blank rises into a slow wave (0 to +-10 px); flat at 0.
variants.reference: opxy/reference/README.md (MNMD MD KIT section drawings, linked) and library/theseus-tower for line weight
variants.risks: Header-wide section (x 160-460) leaves a lot of thin horizontal lines; the lacquer hatching is close to the 3 px floor (5 px spacing, hairline) and could smear on the panel. Rumble's platter line is 420 px long, so as a mutable outline it needs four 64-point runs or it has to be re-thought as a few translated segments. wear's chips are small (3-4 px) and only appear on the 3-4 cut grooves at groove 0. Effects get no note input, so nothing answers playing: the drawing only moves when a knob turns.

variants.subject: The lathe drawn side-on as an engineering elevation on the left, with the groove wall as it plays back traced on the right.
controls: cut: shape - the played trace's amplitude grows and its peaks flatten into plateaus as the cutter saturates (nodes 3-4).
groove: position - the cutter head (node 0) travels along the cantilevered rail from the rim toward the spindle, 56 px, and the radius dimension under the plinth lengthens with it.
wear: count - crackle ticks appear above the trace, 0 to 16, a click per tick; none at 0.
rumble: shape - the trace's grey centre line (nodes 1-2) bends into a slow 1.2-cycle wave, 0 to +-12 px; flat at 0.
variants.reference: opxy/reference/README.md (MNMD FM STAT / VO-6 split layout, linked)
variants.risks: Two places to look; the left elevation only carries groove, so knobs 1, 3 and 4 all act on the right half and P7's column split doesn't hold. The elevation's plinth, rail and column are boxes and could tip into a 'panel' look. Two languages in one frame (elevation, trace) must share weights. The trace is 200 px, so cut needs two mutable paths and rumble two more: all four paths spent. No note input on an effect, so the trace never scrolls; it is a picture of one turn, not a scope.

variants.subject: A sector of the record side seen from above as a survey plan, the groove being cut drawn bright across it among the grey earlier turns, with chainage marks.
controls: cut: shape - the bright groove's lateral swing grows (about 3 to 9 px) and its crests square off as the cutter saturates (nodes 0-2).
groove: position - the label's edge, an arc below the groove, rises from off-frame to just under the cut (~60 px) as the cut moves inward.
wear: count - spot marks (pits, dust) are plotted along the lands and grooves, 0 to ~20; none at 0.
rumble: position - the set of earlier turns slides off-centre against the bright groove (0 to 24 px), an eccentric, wandering side; concentric at 0.
variants.reference: opxy/reference/README.md (stock 'wavetable': one bright trace on black)
variants.risks: P3's own pitfall: it could read as a wiggly line rather than a record unless the curvature and earlier turns stay. The bright groove spans 370 px, so cut uses three of the four mutable paths. groove's label arc is off-frame at the default (0), so the rest frame doesn't show where groove is; it only reads once turned. rumble moves five static arcs as one group: five nodes but a whole-width change. Grid crosses must stay faint or they read as icons.

variants.subject: Five section slices taken across the side from rim to label, stacked diagonally like a patent figure, the slice under the stylus lit and the inner ones carrying shorter waves.
controls: cut: shape - the lit slice's grooved top edge (nodes 0-1) swells and flattens at its crests.
groove: position + shade - which slice is lit steps from the front (rim, 10) to the back (label, 18), easing through the grey between; the lit outline and edge move with it (~140 px diagonal travel).
wear: count - nicks are struck into the lit slice's hatched face and edge, 0 to ~12; none at 0.
rumble: position - the five slices ride a slow vertical wave, up to +-10 px each, so the stack goes out of line; aligned at 0.
variants.risks: groove steps between five slices, so between them it must ease (shade fade plus moving the lit edge) or it reads as on/off. Hatching at 4 px is near the 3 px floor and covers five faces: it's static, but it could smear on the panel. The physics is a little abstract: the player has to know that inner grooves carry shorter waves. Reference numerals (10-18) are patent convention and mean nothing to a player; they're decoration in the language.

variants.subject: The lathe itself, assembled in hidden-line isometric: plinth, platter and lacquer, the rail behind and the cutter head hanging over the disc on its arm.
controls: cut: scale - the swarf thread coiling from the stylus up to the suction tube grows from ~0.7x to 2x (node 2).
groove: position - the carriage, arm and head slide along the rail from the rim toward the spindle (~34 px on screen) and the cut band of turns widens behind it.
wear: count - dust specks settle on the lacquer, 0 to 14; none at 0.
rumble: rotation - the lacquer's top outline turns in plane about the spindle, up to ~30 deg, so the disc reads as wobbling on a worn bearing; still at 0.
variants.risks: Stretch, and it mostly doesn't fit: P11 works because the instrument's parts are what the note selects (theseus' tiers); here no note selects anything and an effect gets no note input, so the 'stack' is just a portrait of the machine. The exception case is recognition: a lathe reads as a turntable at a glance, so the player knows which part is the head, the disc and the plinth without a legend. Against it: the drawing is about the machine, not the sound; cut's swarf coil is tiny at rest (under ~10 px) and hard to see; rumble's in-plane rotation of an ellipse is a fake tilt that may look like the disc sliding off the platter, and 30 deg is a lot; risk of reading as a stock-style product drawing next to TE's own objects.

rejection.reason: Five new unique variations; include a lathe profile view (the workpiece's profile turning on the lathe).
